model.architecture: Falcon-H1 is TII's hybrid design: every one of the 36 layers runs a grouped-query attention branch and a Mamba2 selective-scan branch in parallel on the same input and sums them.

variants.quantization: int8 dynamic on linears + embedding (convs and the scan stay float); fp32 activations declared for GPU

recommended.reason: measured on one Pixel 8a: GPU 11.8 tok/s decode / 23.6 prefill (model card row 2026-09-05, litert_lm_main built from the v0.16.0 tag, 19-token prompt) against CPU 22.46-25.86 tok/s decode / 89.6-98.7 prefill, peak 1374 MB, init 4.5 s (S7 Android backfill 2026-09-05, 2 cold runs). The GPU figure is the card's row, taken with a different binary and a 19-token prompt, so the two are not a same-protocol pair: the CPU's 2.0x higher decode under the 205-token protocol reverses the earlier GPU choice as an indicated ordering, not a measured win; a same-binary GPU run on this phone would settle it; the class moves from midrange-2023+ to midrange because a CPU path carries no SoC-generation constraint

measured on one Galaxy S26 with one binary: GPU 28.81 tok/s decode / 386.7 prefill, peak 2613 MB, init 11.3 s (S4 GPU gate 2026-08-24, 1 run) against CPU 32.14-40.48 decode / 217.1-316.8 prefill, peak 1408 MB, init 1.8 s (S7 Android backfill 2026-09-05, 2 cold runs). Same-device CPU control taken: the CPU decodes 1.3x faster than the GPU on this handset, so the earlier GPU choice is reversed; gpu keeps the prefill advantage for prompt-heavy, short-output work

platform_notes: GPU execution is verified on macOS (Metal), iPhone 17 Pro (Metal), Pixel 8a (Arm Mali, OpenCL) and Qualcomm Adreno (Galaxy S26).
On low-end Android the GPU buys prefill and time-to-first-token, not decode (decode is memory-bandwidth-bound; CPU reads int8 weights, the fp32-activation GPU path reads expanded ones).
GPU runs with fp32 activations (declared in the bundle) — hence the GPU memory multiple (2.50 GB vs 0.66 GB on iPhone).
Multi-length prefill signatures (1–1024) are exported so the runtime picks tight chunks; the bundle carries the tokenizer and the stock ChatML-style Falcon-H1 chat template.
Usage example runs the GPU backend with `--backend gpu --cache no`.

Not a measured row: card reports iPhone 17 Pro gpu prefill_tps 365.9, decode_tps 52.7, ttft_s 0.46 (Performance — On device table (iPhone 17 Pro, cold start, single runs); runtime/run count not stated)

known_issues: 8-question sanity gate: int8 = float = GPU answer 6/8; the two misses ("merci" and 8×7) are the 0.5B model's own level, not conversion or quantization damage.
At 0.5B the model is weak at arithmetic and non-English trivia; int8 adds borderline greedy flips on exactly those items (e.g. 8×7 differs between backends). No degeneracy.
iPhone 17 Pro (Metal) runs the composite quality probe at 7/8.
